headline_tag: uptrend intact, but price is idling below its 50-day line

action.title: SCALE UP acquisition budget
action.detail: The model's budget posture is to scale up acquisition: the long-run uptrend is solid, so this is a phase where spending to win new and returning users has historically paid back best, especially among active traders rather than stablecoin-only users. Because price is pausing just below its 50-day average and the Fed decides on 28 October, the sensible way to apply it is in steps, adding spend gradually and reviewing weekly rather than all at once. This is a budget-timing guide for the business, not trading advice.

reasons: BTC is about 10% above its 200-day average, which is still rising.
Price is up about 26% over 90 days; 77% of those days closed above the long-term average.
Price ($80,165) sits just below the 50-day average ($81,821), so the shorter picture is pausing.
Still about 36% below the all-time high: an early recovery, not a late-stage run.
watch: Price swings are about as calm as they have been in years and the mood reading is a flat 50, yet price sits just under its 50-day average with the Fed deciding tomorrow. A close back above $81,821 would ease that tension; a slide toward $75,383 would start a drop signal.
analysis: Bottom line: the bigger trend still points up, but Bitcoin is idling just under a line that matters, with the Fed decision due tomorrow. Short term, the mood is dead neutral: the Fear & Greed reading sits at exactly 50 and day-to-day price swings are among the calmest of recent years, even as US Bitcoin funds saw about $487M leave on the latest day. If price closes above $81,821 (the 50-day average) the short term turns clearly up, below $72,992 (the 200-day average) it turns down, and in between expect choppy days. A clean move after the Fed would give this week a direction; until then a calm, explain-the-news tone fits better than hype.

Over the next month, the picture leans moderately up. Price is about 26% higher than three months ago and about three in four of the last 90 days finished above the long-term average, but at about $80,200 it has slipped under the 50-day average. Price first needs to win back $81,821 (the 50-day average); above $86,603 (the 90-day high) there is room to climb. News is adding a little: South Korea is leaning toward delaying its 22% crypto tax a fourth time, and US lawmakers agreed another detail of the CLARITY Act (both PANews). The Fed meeting on 27-28 October and US GDP and inflation data later this week are the next scheduled tests; reclaiming the 50-day line after them would keep growth campaigns well timed.

Over three to six months, the trend leans up with the most confidence of the three. Price is about 10% above its 200-day average, which is still rising slowly, and about 36% below its record, so this reads as an early recovery rather than a late-stage run. The recovery stays intact while price holds above $72,992 (the 200-day average), with $67,366 (the 200-week average) as the next floor and $124,753 (the all-time high) as the far marker. A faster-rising 200-day average would strengthen this read and support steady spending on new users; a close back under it would weaken it.
